items.title: 美国中期选举后数据中心民意反弹引发AI股暴跌
items.description: 作者复盘美股AI板块大跌，纳斯达克盘中跌超5%，费城半导体指数一度跌近11%，英伟达跌近9%，纳指一天蒸发近1.8万亿美元市值。背景是中期选举民主党拿下两院，亚利桑那州众议员安萨里提出应暂停先进AI开发，此前桑德斯等人在9月提过《2026年禁止人工超级智能法案》，按训练算力10的25次方划线并规定违规个人最高判20年、公司可强制解散。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ulp3wiu0wqc134cllhoas33kw

items.description: 美国中期选举民主党拿下参众两院，多场竞选以问责 AI 公司为主题，行业面临监管、数据中心建设放缓等前景。44 项地方数据中心暂停提案中 43 项通过，NBC 民调显示 76% 选民反对在社区建数据中心；专家称共和党禁止州级 AI 限制的尝试可能终结，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 未置评，据华尔街日报报道 CEO 们在私下讨论算力容量受限问题。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/vkfrtci1ufbtbydsqersys6lx

items.author: 张子豪
items.content: 比如，一个第三方平台声称接入了旗舰模型，后台却换成便宜的小模型、旧模型，光看回答的语气和质量，我们很难判断；又或者是同一道题目，官网能做出来，用中转站却卡住了。 一个看起来简单的模型请求，背后需要经过「用户—中转站—上游服务商—模型」多个环节，只要其中一环缺少透明度，我们就很难确认自己买到的，是不是标价对应的模型。 这套名为 FlashProve 的开源研究原型，可以为模型推理生成密码学证明。它尝试让服务商为模型的计算结果提供密码学证明，用户不用拿到模型权重，也不用自己再跑一遍大模型，就能核验。 除了使用模型厂商官方的应用，和从官网调用 API 进行对话，我们能确认使用模型的情况。在大多数的 API 调用里，我们提交问题，服务器返回回答，模型世界上是跑在了远程的机器上，我们无法得知后台究竟进行了那些计算。 斯坦福大学的研究项目《Model Equality Testing》曾经就测试过 2024 年四款 Llama 模型的 31 个商业 API 端点，发现其中 11 个端点的输出分布，与 Meta 发布权重的参考分布存在统计差异。 同一个模型名字，有时候并不能对应同一种表现。即便在服务页面挂着的都是 Opus 5.5，但根本无法保证用户获得完全相同的模型。

items.title: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google
items.description: The deal highlights the challenges of developing massive AI data centers.
items.author: Marina Temkin
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. Crusoe, an eight-year-old, Denver-based data center developer recently valued at $30.9 billion , confirmed Friday it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. Google, which Crusoe had tried and failed to land as a customer for the project, is taking over the development after reportedly raising concerns about its cost and construction timeline under Crusoe’s management. Crusoe initially announced the project last year with Blackstone-backed infrastructure company Tallgrass, planning to eventually scale it to 10 gigawatts of power capacity. Google did not disclose how much it paid Crusoe for the unfinished project, but it announced plans to invest $17 billion to develop the data center campus.

OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion. Bloomberg reported on the new funding on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The $11 billion is part of a larger funding round that hasn’t closed yet, according to the outlet. items.title: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web
items.description: Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the penetration testing tool Artex exposed to the internet, allowing anyone access to the hacking tool.
items.author: Zack Whittaker
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. Security researchers have discovered hundreds of copies of a Chinese-made AI hacking tool publicly exposed to the internet for anyone to access, potentially allowing outsiders to launch cyberattacks against unsuspecting targets. The hacking software, called Artex, is an open source autonomous penetration testing tool, meaning software that automatically probes computer systems for weaknesses, and it’s been linked to several cyberattacks since its public release in July. As open source software, it’s free for anyone to download and run on their own servers, making it a popular tool for those who cannot access Anthropic or OpenAI’s most advanced cybersecurity AI models for discovering security vulnerabilities. Microsoft has previously described Artex as a system of AI agents that can conduct cyberattacks “from reconnaissance through data exfiltration with little needed human interaction.” In a blog post , cybersecurity firm Censys, which scans the internet for exposed or vulnerable systems, said that it identified more than 800 distinct deployments of Artex that were accessible from the web without needing a password to log in. Silas Cutler, principal security researcher at Censys who wrote the blog post, said that not every instance of Artex is operated maliciously and many are used for authorized testers

items.title: Meta introduces Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent
items.description: Meta's Muse agents continue to get new features and integrations. Spaces promises to be a new way to interact with the AI helpers.
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. Meta recently launched its Muse agents — a new generation of cuddly agentic helpers. Now, the company has launched Spaces, a new way to communicate and collaborate with them. As far as I can tell, Spaces are basically breakout conversations that revolve around a particular topic — although Meta refers to them as “custom experiences.” They live in the sidebar of the interface where you interact with your Muse agent. Clicking on the Space brings up the conversation, where Muse works toward a particular goal on your behalf. For instance, if you wanted to plan a vacation, you could open a new Space focused on that particular project, and whenever you want to work on it with Muse, you would click to open that particular tab. Or, if you’re focused on collecting recipes for an upcoming family event, you’d open a new Space for that particular project. Other examples Meta gives are a holiday gift tracker, a wedding planner, or a space for DIY projects. “Describe an idea in chat, and Muse builds a space for you, whether that’s a tracker, a planner or a project board,” Meta says.
